question: Should WhatsApp now require every injected media reader to provide explicit local roots, and may the existing WhatsApp runtime loader export be removed in the same release?
rationale: The stricter boundary fixes a concrete access-widening problem but intentionally changes shipped failure behavior and removes an intentional runtime API surface, so owner intent and supported-consumer knowledge are required.

options.title: Require explicit roots with migration proof
options.body: Keep the fail-closed boundary, rebase the branch, migrate all supported callers, and prove that the removed runtime export has no remaining contract consumers.

options.title: Stage the contract change
options.body: Land the canonical primitives first while temporarily preserving a documented runtime compatibility surface, then remove it through an explicit deprecation path.

options.title: Accept the immediate break
options.body: Land the fail-closed behavior and export removal as-is after explicitly accepting that older injected-reader integrations may stop sending media.

recommendation.title: Require explicit roots with migration proof
recommendation.body: Keep the fail-closed boundary, rebase the branch, migrate all supported callers, and prove that the removed runtime export has no remaining contract consumers.

likelyOwner.reason: Their earlier merged work introduced the shared outbound-media and media-root contracts whose upgrade boundary must be confirmed.
